newsitem.title: UK: NWE high, low sulphur fuel oil edge upwards.
newsitem.headline: NWE high, low sulphur fuel oil edge upwards.

text.p: NWE high and low sulphur cracked fuel oil prices were slightly firmer on Monday as crude futures strengthened and colder weather buoyed sentiment, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $110 fob ARA in the morning, then at $113 fob Rotterdam and $113 fob Antwerp. "Very quiet," one ARA player said. Low sulphur barges were not heard traded.
High sulphur cargo activity was thin but swaps were a shade up. Jan was bid at $115.50 cif NWE. In the Mediterranean, Jan cargo swaps were up in a range between $106 and $107.50 fob Med.
"It is more weather related than anything else," one dealer said.
Low sulphur cargo prices were notionally little changed and swaps levels were pegged at around $124/$125 fob NWE for Jan.

These numbers follow last week's physical trades at $124 and $125 fob NWE for two pieces sold out of Scandinavia, sold by two different refiners to two different traders. At least two more availabilities, one of which was of high density low sulphur material, were not being actively offered, traders said.
Denmark's state-owned oil marketing company Daufas ceases trading on Tuesday, after having sustained losses in the past couple of years from paper trading activities.
